title: Go SDK: schema-driven codec + union-dispatch decoders and streaming hedge/retry examples
creator: Ayesha Banerjee
description: Introduce a small library in the Go SDK that provides schema-driven codec helpers: typed struct mapping, union-dispatch decoders (for choices/variants), and ergonomic streaming examples that combine incremental NDJSON parsing with hedged retries and graceful fallback mappings.
background: We frequently see teams building ad-hoc decoders when integrating streaming model outputs (NDJSON/line-delimited JSON) that include variant envelopes (e.g., {type: "choice", payload: {...}}). Current SDK helpers are focused on envelope-oriented adapters but lack a concise schema-driven union dispatcher and examples for mixing hedged retries (duplicate streaming requests with fastest-complete response) with incremental decode and backoff. This causes duplicated code and brittle backwards-compatibility handling across customers.
goals: 1) Provide a small, well-documented set of generic helpers to decode union/variant shapes into strongly-typed Go structs with minimal boilerplate. 2) Offer a canonical streaming example that shows how to: open a streaming response, decode NDJSON incrementally, run a hedged retry (select first non-error), and apply graceful fallback mappers for missing fields/backcompat. 3) Add unit + integration tests and a benchmark for throughput/latency on typical 1–2k token outputs.
non_goals: Add support for codecs other than JSON/NDJSON (no protobuf/avro); build platform-level hedging in runtime — this is an SDK-level sample for client-side hedging only.
proposal: Implement a package internal/codec with three exported primitives: 1) Register[T any](key string, decoder func(map[string]any) (T, error)) - a registry for variant dispatch; 2) DecodeUnion[T any](raw map[string]any) (T, error) - dispatcher that reads 'kind'/'type' fields and invokes registered decoder; 3) StreamDecoder[T any](r io.Reader, handle func(T) error) - incremental NDJSON decoder with backpressure-safe buffering. Provide hedged helper in examples/hedged_stream.go that concurrently starts two requests with slightly staggered timing and returns the first successful stream while cancelling the other. Include fallback mapper utilities to coerce missing fields or older envelope shapes into current typed structs.
design_notes: - Use Go 1.20/1.21 generics (type parameters) and avoid reflection-heavy paths except for the initial map[string]any -> typed struct conversion. - Decoder registry keys will be a small stable string (e.g., "openapi.choice.v1"). - For incremental NDJSON parsing we'll reuse a bufio.Scanner with a custom split for large JSON objects to avoid tokenization mistakes; fall back to json.Decoder for strict decode when line parsing fails. - Hedged example uses context cancellation and a fan-in channel; first non-nil error is returned only if both streams fail. - Backcompat mappers registered as functions that can be applied in a pipeline to transform older envelopes to the canonical map shape before dispatch.
implementation_plan: 1) Add internal/codec package with registry and dispatch primitives (3 days). 2) Implement StreamDecoder and NDJSON split helper + tests for edge cases (2 days). 3) Write hedged_stream example and integration test against a local test server that emits delayed NDJSON fragments (1 day). 4) Add benchmarks and micro-bench harness (1 day). 5) Docs, examples, and PR for review (1 day).
acceptance_criteria: - The codec registry compiles under Go 1.20+ and is covered by unit tests with >= 90% branch coverage. - StreamDecoder can handle multi-line JSON objects and recovers when encountering invalid partial lines (test cases provided). - Hedged_stream example demonstrates starting two requests and returning the first successful stream; integration test asserts cancellation of the loser. - Benchmark shows no >20% regression in decode throughput compared to current naive decoder for a 2k token NDJSON stream. - PR has +2 approvals (one from SDK lead, one from runtime/infra engineer) and a linked integration run on CI.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for registry: register/unregister, duplicate key handling, unknown key error. - Stream tests: chunked input, interleaved newlines inside strings, truncated lines, and malformed JSON recovery. - Hedged tests: simulated slow writer, failing writer, and both-writers-fail case. - Fuzz harness for StreamDecoder with random bytes to guard against panic. - Benchmark for 1000/2000 token outputs comparing existing decoder and new StreamDecoder.
docs: - Add a new section in SDK docs: "Streaming & Structured Output" with code snippets for: registry usage, union decoder patterns, hedged streaming example, and backcompat mapping. - Include GoDoc comments on exported helpers. - Short migration guide for teams using ad-hoc decoders.
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Created initial RFC sketch and shared on #sdk-dev. Early feedback: prefer map->struct via encoding/json with validation hooks rather than full reflection mappers. Marking estimate 5 pts.
2025-01-17: Prototype registry + simple union dispatch implemented locally. Ran into edge case where some envelopes use "type" and others use "kind"; added pre-dispatch normalization step (mapper).

2025-01-18: Implemented NDJSON split helper; found bufio.Scanner default token limit hit on ~350KB objects, added custom buffer growth and test for large object. Ran first benchmark; naive decoder still slightly faster on tiny messages but memory overhead acceptable for streaming cases.
2025-01-20: Hedged example implemented and integration test added. CI failing on flaky cancellation in racey test; added synchronization to test harness and re-ran CI locally.
2025-01-20: Open question for review: should registry be public package or internal? Suggested internal for now and evaluate after adoption.
decisions: Keep registry internal by default (internal/codec) to allow API iteration without semver constraints.
Use 'type' then 'kind' then 'schema' fallback chain for union dispatch normalization.
Expose hedged example as examples/hedged_stream.go not as exported helper; keep helper primitives small and composable.
open_questions: If adoption grows, when do we promote registry to top-level package? Add to roadmap to revisit after 3 customers adopt?
Do we want a small opt-in reflection path for automatic struct population (tag-driven) versus explicit decoder functions? Tradeoff: convenience vs. control/validation.
follow_ups: Link migration guide to internal playbook and run 2 office hours with SDK adopters (owners: Ayesha + Miguel).
Add telemetry counters to StreamDecoder example (items-decoded, decode-errors, avg-latency) and discuss adding to Console observability later.
qa_checklist: Unit tests pass locally and on CI.
Integration hedged test stable for 50 runs.
Bench numbers added to PR comment and compared to baseline.
Docs snippet reviewed by DE (Developer Experience) lead.
release_notes_draft: Added internal codec helpers to the Go SDK to simplify decoding variant envelopes and streaming NDJSON parsing. Includes an examples/hedged_stream demonstrating client-side hedged streaming with cancellation and graceful fallback mapping for legacy envelopes.
